name: Shang oracle-bone writing
description: Written inscriptions on oracle bones associated with late Shang Chinese divination, an early attestation of a Chinese writing tradition.

impact.note: Earliest attested Chinese writing, ancestral to the script East Asian societies governed, recorded and studied with for three millennia; scored as the origin, not the bones.

date.label: late 14th century BCE
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: The Metropolitan Museum dates the beginning of writings engraved on oracle bones to the late fourteenth century BCE.
events.caveats: The Metropolitan Museum says late fourteenth century BCE without numerical bounds or a particular bone; the century-wide bounds avoid imposing a precise half-century. This is a retrospective date for a scribal tradition, not the invention date.

evidence.supports: The museum places writings on oracle bones beginning in the late fourteenth century BCE.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

caveats: The source establishes a documented Chinese scribal tradition, not whether all antecedents arose independently of other scripts.

research.note: Second reader checked the museum retrospective. The source does not identify a specific bone or quantify late-century boundaries.
